    Pool effect sizes with common-effect or random-effects models

    Source: R/meta-pool.R
    meta_pool.Rd

    meta_pool() combines study level effect sizes into an overall estimate using inverse variance weights. The between-study variance \(\tau^2\) can be estimated by restricted maximum likelihood ("REML", the default), maximum likelihood ("ML"), the DerSimonian-Laird method of moments ("DL"), the Paule-Mandel generalised Q estimator ("PM") or the Sidik-Jonkman estimator ("SJ"). method = "FE" fits a common-effect (fixed effect) model.

    Usage

    meta_pool(
  .data,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  method = "REML",
  test = "z",
  level = 0.95,
  study = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A <meta_es> from meta_effect_size() or any data frame with effect sizes and sampling variances.

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    method

    Estimator of the between-study variance: "REML", "ML", "DL", "PM", "SJ" or "FE" (common effect).

    test

    "z" for normal based inference or "hksj" for the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    study

    <data-masking> Optional study labels. Taken from the <meta_es> when available.

    Value

    A <meta_fit> with one row, term = "overall".

    Details

    With test = "hksj", the standard error is rescaled by the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman factor and inference uses a t distribution with \(k - 1\) degrees of freedom. A prediction interval for the effect in a new study, \(\hat\mu \pm c \sqrt{SE^2 + \hat\tau^2}\), is always reported, where \(c\) is the normal or t quantile that matches test. A Q-profile confidence interval for \(\tau^2\) (Viechtbauer, 2007) is stored and returned by glance().

    The estimators are implemented directly in base R and match the results of metafor::rma() to numerical precision.

    References

    DerSimonian, R. and Laird, N. (1986). Meta-analysis in clinical trials. Controlled Clinical Trials, 7(3), 177-188. doi:10.1016/0197-2456(86)90046-2

    Paule, R. C. and Mandel, J. (1982). Consensus values and weighting factors. Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards, 87(5), 377-385. doi:10.6028/jres.087.022

    Sidik, K. and Jonkman, J. N. (2005). Simple heterogeneity variance estimation for meta-analysis. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C, 54(2), 367-384. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9876.2005.00489.x

    Hartung, J. and Knapp, G. (2001). A refined method for the meta-analysis of controlled clinical trials with binary outcome. Statistics in Medicine, 20(24), 3875-3889. doi:10.1002/sim.1009

    Viechtbauer, W. (2007). Confidence intervals for the amount of heterogeneity in meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 26(1), 37-52. doi:10.1002/sim.2514

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg,
  event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg,
  study = author
)
meta_pool(bcg)
#> # Meta-analysis <meta_fit>
#> # Model: random effects, restricted maximum likelihood
#> # Measure: log risk ratio; k = 13
#> # tau^2 = 0.3132; I^2 = 92.22%; H^2 = 12.86
#> # Q(12) = 152.23, p < 0.0001
#> # 95% prediction interval: [-1.8667, 0.4376]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term    estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 overall   -0.715     0.180     -3.97 0.0000705    -1.07    -0.362
meta_pool(bcg, method = "DL", test = "hksj")
#> # Meta-analysis <meta_fit>
#> # Model: random effects, DerSimonian-Laird
#> # Measure: log risk ratio; k = 13
#> # tau^2 = 0.3088; I^2 = 92.12%; H^2 = 12.69
#> # Q(12) = 152.23, p < 0.0001
#> # 95% prediction interval: [-1.9872, 0.5590]
#> # Inference: Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman t tests (df = 12)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term    estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 overall   -0.714     0.181     -3.95 0.00192    -1.11    -0.320
meta_pool(bcg, method = "FE") |> glance()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 21
#>   model_type  nobs method test   tau2 tau2.low tau2.high   tau    I2    H2    R2
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>  <chr> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 pool          13 FE     z         0       NA        NA     0  92.1  12.7    NA
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: QE <dbl>, df.residual <int>, p.QE <dbl>, QM <dbl>,
#> #   p.QM <dbl>, pred.low <dbl>, pred.high <dbl>, logLik <dbl>, AIC <dbl>,
#> #   BIC <dbl>
